newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker but auction well received.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker but auction well received.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Wednesday, despite a well received auction of three-year government bonds, after stronger-than-expected U.S. consumer credit data pulled bonds there lower, analysts said.

"It's primarily the direction of the U.S. market right now. We've seen the U.S. market quite weak with consumer credit numbers coming out," said a dealer at one bank-owned brokerage. "People are very nervous about having long positions going into the end of the week."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.40 to C$107.80 to yield 7.327 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 21/32 to yield 6.84 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 49 basis points from 50 basis points at Tuesday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. bonds weakened this afternoon after the U.S. Federal Reserve reported U.S. consumer credit grew a higher-than-expected US$7.4 billion in November, a 7.4 percent annual rate.
"The bond market is pricing in a scenario on the economy that is a lot stronger than many analysts had believed," said Philip Strathy, chief investment officer with Strathy Investments Ltd.
Canadian bonds closed lower even though the afternoon auction of C$2.7 billion of 5.5 percent Government of Canada bonds due February 1, 2000 was well received.

The Government of Canada said its C$2.7 billion auction of 5.5 percent bonds due February 1, 2000 produced an average yield of 5.195 percent, with a low yield of 5.187 percent and a high yield of 5.208 percent. Bids from primary dealers totalled C$6,125.85 million.
"The bid to cover ratio was in line and it was well received. Unfortunately, shortly thereafter the market sold off," said Strathy.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.32 to C$101.95 to yield 6.725 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 14 basis points from 12 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.89 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.16 percent.
